pr_title: drivers: spi: stm32 spi driver supporting DMA in asynchronous mode
pr_body:
add the support of the SPI asynchronous mode to the sm32 spi driver with DMA enabled or not
Enable this async mode when running the tests/drivers/spi/spi_loopback 
and add the dma for spi transfer with _overlay-stm32-spi-dma.conf_
This is now the case hen the CONFIG_SPI_STM32_DMA is selected,

The SPI transfer is possible in ASYNC mode is possible CONFIG_SPI_ASYNC=y or not (CONFIG_SPI_ASYNC=n)
--> adding one more config to the tests/drivers/spi/spi_loopback for stm32 serie.

Add the b_l4s5i_iot01a disco kit to the list of supported boards
 
Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/55205

Signed-off-by: Francois Ramu <francois.ramu@st.com>

issue_context.title: spi: stm32 support for asynchronous transfer using DMA
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The SPI STM32 drivers [supports](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/spi/spi_ll_stm32.c#L833) using DMA only for synchronous transfers. The DMA support is needed for high-speed SPI communication. The problem occurs when the chip that runs Zephyr is a SPI slave. The start of a SPI communication is unknown and the `spi_transceive` (which supports DMA) call blocks the program flow. Using ASYNC SPI API would be a much better solution in this case.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The request is to support using DMA also for the asynchronous transfers, as it is done for [UART](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/serial/uart_stm32.c#L1310).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Create a separate thread for the `spi_transceive` blocking call, but it is not the way to go. 

**Additional context**
NA
